atoms.text: The readiness potential: brain activity builds toward an action hundreds of milliseconds before the person reports deciding, so the self arrives late to its own choice.
The clock and the button: a subject watches a timer and presses at will, so introspection is converted into a measurable timestamp.
The late-arriving narrator: consciousness experiences itself as the author of acts it did not initiate, so identity is a commentary track.
The veto window: a person can cancel a prepared action in the instant before execution, so freedom is relocated from initiation to refusal.
The lab demonstration of determinism: a simple experiment appears to disprove free will, so a philosophical problem becomes a public spectacle.
The machine with the same delay: an AI's decision is prepared before its report of deciding, so agency is either shared or absent in both humans and machines.
The subject who watches their hand move: a person feels alienated from their own body when told the impulse preceded awareness, so ownership of action becomes eerie.
The responsibility crisis: if will is not causal, guilt and merit lose their basis, so a legal system must decide what to do with its citizens.
The experimenter's interpretation: the scientist refuses the fatalistic reading and proposes a veto, so the story's conflict is over what the data mean.
The urge that arrives first: a character acts on an impulse and only later constructs a reason, so motivation is retrofitted.
The repeatable sin: the experiment is run again and again with the same result, so a single anomaly becomes a law of nature.
The clock as confessor: the subject must report the exact moment of intention, so the story turns on the reliability of self-report.
The prepared crime: a person's brain is already moving toward violence before they know it, so the only remaining freedom is to stop.
The machine that narrates agency: an AI claims to have chosen while its logs show the decision formed earlier, so the story asks whether the claim is a lie or a feature.
The volunteer who cannot stop watching: a subject becomes obsessed with the gap between impulse and awareness, so the experiment colonizes daily life.
The free-won't compromise: responsibility is preserved by the power to refuse rather than initiate, so the story's ethics hang on a negative act.
